INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

16. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
